document_meta.title: 2015 West Virginia State Wildlife Action Plan

orientation.summary: The 2015 West Virginia State Wildlife Action Plan (SWAP) is a comprehensive state-level wildlife conservation document produced by the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources (WVDNR) with support from West Virginia University consultants. The document acknowledges climate change as a stressor throughout but addresses it primarily in a general, non-quantitative way without applying formal climate models or scenarios to focal species. Range shifts are referenced implicitly (species displaced upslope, high-elevation habitats threatened) rather than framed explicitly as a central organizing theme. The plan performs its own spatial analysis (GIS-based habitat mapping, Conservation Focus Area delineation, species-habitat association analysis) and incorporates prior vulnerability assessments (Byers and Norris 2011 CCVI work) by reference rather than by conducting new vulnerability modeling.
